findings.rationale: Accepted, and fixed with a probe rather than a hedge: --reasoning-effort high and --effort high are each rejected by the frozen CLI with error: unknown option, and the suffixed ids already ran to a result event in 6.1. P12 now cites that behavioral pair. The --help bracket-override syntax is removed from the claim entirely - nothing in this plan uses it and it has no receipt, which is exactly the standard the rubric asks for.

Accepted, and this is the systemic fix the previous two rounds kept approximating. The enabled-id set is now defined once and executably in cursor-model.sh (cursor_enabled_ids / cursor_is_enabled_id); the auto guard calls the predicate instead of carrying a list, and the negative-control test enumerates the same function instead of restating one. Three hand-maintained copies drifting while the test stays green was the real hazard, not any single missing id.

Accepted: the argv said CURSOR_BIN while the same section defined the per-rail contract as BIN with an existing --bin override - an override that could be silently bypassed. One contract now: CURSOR_BIN is dispatch-hetero-local, and both review and author rails use $BIN throughout, including the exact argv.

Accepted, and the generation-2 repair overshot in this respect: it moved resolve-review-loop.sh's allowlists into Phase 2, which admits a cursor roster seat before any review rail exists to execute it. Admission moves back to Phase 3; Phase 2 keeps only the schema and readiness contracts base dispatch needs, and the cross-phase rule - every runner the resolver accepts must be executable by its downstream dispatcher - is asserted at the Phase 3 boundary.

Accepted: declaring Stage 0 met from probes on cursor-grok-4.6-low-fast and then qualifying cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast is precisely the score-transfer-across-scopes error engine-onboarding forbids, and --list-models containment is inventory rather than behavior. G0, G0.5, G1, and G2 are now re-executed on the frozen id with receipts appended before the suite starts.

Accepted and correct: this is the third and narrowest form of the section 1 hole. Section 2.6 said wildcard families while section 3a and the test said exact table rows, and the table rows are non-fast, so --cursor-fast made gpt-5.3-codex-low-fast reachable and unguarded. Resolved by the same single-source repair: the match set is the table closed under fast, computed by cursor_enabled_ids, and every consumer derives from it rather than restating it.
